rows.vgi.doc_md:
# Excel Spreadsheet Read & Write in SQL

![Apache POI logo](https://poi.apache.org/images/project-header.png)

**Query Microsoft Excel workbooks (`.xls` and `.xlsx`) directly from DuckDB SQL — read every cell with its value, type, and formula, and export any query result to a downloadable `.xlsx` file — powered by [Apache POI](https://poi.apache.org/).**

This extension turns spreadsheets into first-class SQL data sources. It is built for data engineers, analysts, and application developers who need to ingest Excel files, inspect workbook structure, or hand results back to spreadsheet users — without leaving SQL or writing glue code in Python or a BI tool. Both the legacy binary `.xls` format (OLE2 / HSSF) and the modern Office Open XML `.xlsx` format (OOXML / XSSF) are supported, and inputs may be supplied either as a file path or as raw `BLOB` bytes already loaded into DuckDB.

Under the hood the worker embeds [Apache POI](https://github.com/apache/poi), the mature, battle-tested Java library for reading and writing Microsoft Office file formats. POI parses the workbook, evaluates formulas, and preserves cell typing (numbers, dates, booleans, strings, and errors), while the worker streams the results back to DuckDB over Apache Arrow. Untrusted spreadsheets are opened behind zip-bomb and decompression-ratio defenses, and external workbook links are never resolved, so importing arbitrary `.xlsx` files stays safe. See the [Apache POI spreadsheet documentation](https://poi.apache.org/components/spreadsheet/) and the [HSSF/XSSF quick guide](https://poi.apache.org/components/spreadsheet/quick-guide.html) for format details.

## Key concepts

- **Rich, cell-level reads.** A workbook is surfaced not as opaque rows but cell by cell, each with its worksheet, position, A1 reference, evaluated value, data type, and (for formula cells) the underlying formula text — so numbers, dates, booleans, strings, errors, and computed values are all preserved and distinguishable.
- **Structure before data.** You can inspect a workbook's worksheet directory — names and dimensions — cheaply, without materializing every cell, then drill into a single sheet.
- **Path or bytes.** Reader inputs may be a filesystem path the worker opens, or raw `BLOB` bytes already loaded into DuckDB, so the same function works on files on disk and on content that arrived over the wire.
- **Round-tripping to Excel.** Any query result can be serialized back into a downloadable `.xlsx` workbook, and raw bytes can be sniffed to confirm their format.

## When to use it

Reach for this worker when you need to ingest spreadsheet exports into an analytical pipeline, audit the sheets and formulas inside a workbook, validate untrusted uploads by content rather than file extension, or hand polished Excel deliverables back to spreadsheet users — all without leaving SQL or writing glue code in Python or a BI tool.
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description":"Read a workbook's non-blank cells (passed as inline bytes).","sql":"SELECT sheet, cell_ref, value, type FROM excel.main.read_excel(from_base64('')) ORDER BY cell_ref;"},{"description":"Export a query result to an .xlsx workbook BLOB and confirm bytes were produced.","sql":"SELECT octet_length(xlsx) > 0 AS produced FROM excel.main.write_xlsx((SELECT 1 AS id, 'Ada' AS name), sheet_name := 'People');"},{"description":"Round-trip: detect that the written bytes are an .xlsx workbook.","sql":"SELECT excel.main.detect_excel(xlsx) AS fmt FROM excel.main.write_xlsx((SELECT 1 AS id, 'Ada' AS name));"}]
